title: Ecosystem
blurb: Neighbors, WEM, analytics pipes, AI handoffs, and a glossary that refuses uncited words.
summary: Every box needs a link. Every word needs a page or a local label.

lessons.title: The domain has neighbors
objectives: Give each one its own failure
paragraphs: A Five9 domain does not live alone. Voice arrives on a SIP story. Agents sit in a desktop. WEM or a partner workforce suite watches the roster. A CRM pops. GenAI Studio may draft a summary. E911 carries a location. Reports leave through a role and an API.
The ecosystem page in this lab is a map of those neighbors with the same citations as the lessons. If a box has no link, it does not belong on the map.

lessons.title: Workforce, quality, and the recording shelf
objectives: Keep quality scores out of the router unless an admin change says so
paragraphs: The WEM product page describes workforce management, quality, analytics, surveys, and recording, and it also describes a Verint partnership. Five9 says it manages install and upgrades for the solution it delivers. The data sheet is the short version of that claim.
Native WEM and a Verint deployment are not interchangeable words. Ask which one is in the contract. Quality scores do not change a skill assignment unless a process says they do.

lessons.title: Analytics and the report that is not a dashboard rumor
objectives: Name the pipe that produced the number
Do not average a wallboard and a report
paragraphs: Analytics shows up on the WEM page and inside reporting. They are not one button. Standard reports need the Reporting role. Categories include ACD Queue, Campaign, Call Log, and the rest of that list. Layouts are tabular, summary, and matrix.
A wallboard that refreshes from Statistics Web Services is an integration. A scheduled summary email is a report. Say which one broke.

lessons.title: AI agents are a handoff with a name
objectives: Give every bot a named exit
Do not invent a model name
paragraphs: Five9 Engage talks about self-service and the agent desktop together. Studio holds a digital IVA task. GenAI Studio is where knowledge and prompts are tested, and the product page says it powers Five9 AI applications, starting with Agent Assist summaries. This lab does not name a default model.
An AI agent that cannot transfer to a real skill is a dead end. The IVR module list includes IVA Transfer. Digital IVA uses a Studio task key placed into VCC. Those are the handoffs you can cite.
uncertain: GenAI Studio's product page describes an engine-agnostic studio and names Agent Assist summaries as an initial consumer. It does not name a default model for this lab to repeat.

lessons.title: CRM, UC, and the desktop are three contracts
objectives: Treat adapter, UC integration, and local UC app as three lines
paragraphs: Plus adapters named in the technical requirements include Salesforce, ServiceNow, Dynamics 365, Zendesk, Oracle, NetSuite, Epic, and the Agent Desktop Toolkit. Zoom Phone and Teams show up as prebuilt paths on the API page. A UC app on the PC is also a bandwidth line, about 320 kbps.
The agent's screen can show a CRM card, a UC window, and Agent Assist at once. When one is blank, name which contract failed.

lessons.title: The glossary is the contract with yourself
objectives: Cite a word or mark it local
Keep campaign profile and user profile apart
paragraphs: Teams lose hours to words that Five9 uses narrowly: domain, skill, campaign profile, DNIS, disposition, list penetration, vertical dialing, campaign, autodial, blended, manual touch. The ecosystem glossary in this lab defines the ones we could cite and marks the rest.
If you cannot point at a page, say 'we use this word locally' and keep it out of a design that claims to be vendor language.

lessons.title: Read the map before you add a box
objectives: Check the integration row before you buy
Split logos that hide two products
paragraphs: Integration maps fail when a logo is enough. Salesforce in the IVR is a module. Salesforce on the desktop is an adapter. Certified Caller is not the ANI. RedSky is not the ITSP. Verint is not automatically your WEM. Studio regions are not Equinix edges.
Open the ecosystem page, filter the glossary, and check the integration table against whatever you are about to buy. If the row is missing, you do not yet have a citation.
